instructions: Class assignment 1 (Modules 1 to 3), set by the Big Data Analytics faculty.
Marks are not printed on the assignment; each answer is written at the length of a 10-mark exam answer, and short definitions at 5 marks.

questions.text: Explain the concept of Big Data in your own words and discuss its significance in today's digital world with suitable examples.
Explain the major characteristics (5 Vs) of Big Data and describe how each characteristic influences data processing.
Explain the core components of Hadoop, namely HDFS and MapReduce, and describe the role of each component in Big Data processing.
Compare traditional data processing approaches with Big Data approaches and analyze their impact on modern business operations.
Design a physical organization of compute nodes for a large-scale enterprise using the principles of distributed file systems, and justify your design.
Demonstrate how file storage can be organized across multiple nodes in a distributed environment using block distribution and replication techniques.
Given a suitable dataset, implement the Map phase of the MapReduce framework to extract key-value pairs and explain the generated output.
Illustrate how the Shuffle and Sort phase groups data by key and demonstrate how the Reduce phase aggregates the grouped data in a MapReduce workflow.
Demonstrate how the fault tolerance features of the MapReduce framework ensure uninterrupted data processing during node failures.
Apply the MapReduce framework to perform selection (filtering) operations on a large dataset and explain the execution process.
Analyze the reasons why modern enterprises adopt NoSQL databases instead of traditional RDBMS for specific workloads, and discuss the business drivers behind this shift.
Compare the scalability models of NoSQL and Relational Databases, and analyze how these models influence business decisions and system performance.
Compare the schema design approaches of NoSQL and Relational Databases, and analyze their impact on business agility, application development, and data management.
